summary: AI has already delivered real-world drug repurposing breakthroughs; biology is a major near-term AI application
summary_extended: Baker argues that AI has already demonstrated concrete, life-saving value in drug repurposing, citing a personal anecdote in which a friend used AI to identify that an existing 50-60 year old drug could effectively treat a rare pediatric disease affecting approximately 10,000 children per year. He presents this as evidence that AI's near-term impact on biology and medicine is underappreciated by the market, which he believes is too focused on infrastructure and compute as the primary value drivers. Baker views AI-driven drug repurposing — applying existing approved compounds to new indications — as a particularly high-value, near-term application because it bypasses much of the traditional drug development timeline and cost. The investment implication is broadly constructive on AI applied to biology, though Baker does not name specific companies or stocks in this segment, making the thesis more of a thematic directional view than an actionable single-stock call.
detail: Baker references a personal anecdote of a friend using AI to identify that an existing 50-60 year old drug could effectively cure a rare pediatric disease affecting ~10,000 children/year. He views AI-driven drug repurposing as an underappreciated near-term value driver for the AI industry.
